name: Octavia E. Butler Landing
summary: This is where Perseverance touched down on 18 February 2021. NASA named the spot after the science fiction author Octavia E. Butler.
detail: The rover made its first test drive from here on 4 March 2021: 4 m forward, a turn on the spot, then 2.5 m back, 6.5 m in all.

photos.caption: Navcam view from Perseverance on sol 9 (28 February 2021), parked at its landing site.
Navcam view from Perseverance on sol 9 (28 February 2021), parked at its landing site.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 11 (2 March 2021), parked at its landing site.

name: Wright Brothers Field
summary: Ingenuity made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet here on 19 April 2021. It rose 3 m, hovered for 30 seconds and landed, 39 seconds in all.
detail: NASA named the airfield after the Wright brothers. Perseverance watched from Van Zyl Overlook, about 64 m away, and passed the helicopter's data on to Earth.

photos.caption: Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 58 (19 April 2021), from Van Zyl Overlook, about 64 m away. Ingenuity stands on Wright Brothers Field on the day of its first flight.
Navcam view from Perseverance on sol 58 (19 April 2021), parked at Van Zyl Overlook, about 64 m from the helicopter, on the day of the first flight.

name: Roubion
summary: Perseverance tried to drill its first rock core here on 6 August 2021. The rock crumbled, so the sealed tube holds only Martian air.
detail: The drill and the sampling system did what they were told: the rock was old, changed by water and too weak to hold together. The tube became the mission's one sample of the atmosphere, and the team moved on to a harder rock, Rochette.

photos.caption: Navcam view from Perseverance on sol 164 (6 August 2021), parked at Roubion.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 163 (5 August 2021), parked at Roubion.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 163 (5 August 2021), parked at Roubion.

name: Rochette
summary: Rochette is the rock that gave Perseverance its first two rock cores, in September 2021. It is basalt, a volcanic rock that may have formed from lava flows.
detail: The cores are named Montdenier and Montagnac. They hold salts, a sign that water was in contact with this rock for a long time, and the salts may have trapped tiny bubbles of ancient water.

photos.caption: Navcam view from Perseverance on sol 190 (1 September 2021), parked at Rochette.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 194 (5 September 2021), parked at Rochette.

name: Séítah
summary: Séítah is a stretch of ridges, sand dunes and boulders on the crater floor. At the Brac outcrop here, the rover found rock packed with large olivine crystals that grew in slowly cooling magma.
detail: It is not yet known whether that magma cooled in a thick lava lake on the surface or in a chamber underground. The rocks here also met water more than once. Two cores, Salette and Coulettes, were drilled from Brac in November 2021.

photos.caption: Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 265 (17 November 2021), parked at the Brac outcrop in South Séítah.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 265 (18 November 2021), parked at the Brac outcrop in South Séítah.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 265 (18 November 2021), parked at the Brac outcrop in South Séítah.

name: Jezero delta front
summary: This is the foot of the delta, a fan of rock and sediment at the western edge of Jezero crater. It formed billions of years ago where a river ran into the crater's lake.
detail: Perseverance reached the delta on 13 April 2022 after crossing about 5 km of crater floor in 31 sols. NASA calls the delta one of the best places on Mars to look for signs of past microscopic life.

photos.caption: Navcam view from Perseverance on sol 423 (29 April 2022), parked at the foot of the delta.
Navcam view from Perseverance on sol 423 (29 April 2022), parked at the foot of the delta.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 424 (30 April 2022), parked at the foot of the delta.

name: Wildcat Ridge
summary: Wildcat Ridge is a rock about 1 m wide, made of mud and fine sand that settled in a salty lake billions of years ago. In it the rover's SHERLOC instrument made its strongest detection of organic molecules up to then.
detail: Organic molecules are carbon compounds. They can form with or without life, so they are not proof of life. Two cores, Hazeltop and Bearwallow, were drilled here in July and August 2022. A nearby sandstone, Skinner Ridge, carries grains that came from far outside the crater.

photos.caption: Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 507 (24 July 2022), parked at Wildcat Ridge.

name: Observation Mountain
summary: Here the rover took its first two samples of loose Martian soil, in December 2022. They came from a low ripple of dust, sand and pebbles shaped by the wind.
detail: Wind carries fine grains a long way, so the soil can hold material from well beyond this spot. It also helps show how Martian dust will act on spacecraft and on astronauts. The samples are named Atmo Mountain and Crosswind Lake.

photos.caption: Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 635 (3 December 2022), parked at Observation Mountain.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 635 (3 December 2022), parked at Observation Mountain.

name: Three Forks sample depot
summary: Perseverance laid ten sample tubes on the ground here in December 2022 and January 2023. They are a backup set, in case the rover cannot hand over the samples it carries.
detail: The depot holds one sample from each pair taken up to then, one tube of Martian air and one witness tube, set out in a zigzag. The last tube was dropped on 28 January 2023. The rover first came to Three Forks on 13 April 2022, when it reached the delta.

photos.caption: Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 690 (28 January 2023), parked at the Three Forks sample depot.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 690 (28 January 2023), parked at the Three Forks sample depot.
Navcam view from Perseverance on sol 688 (26 January 2023), parked at the Three Forks sample depot.

name: Berea
summary: Berea is a rock on top of the delta, cored on 30 March 2023. Scientists think it is made of material that an ancient river carried here.
detail: The rock is rich in carbonate, a mineral that forms in liquid water. On Earth, carbonate rocks keep a long record of climate and can preserve fossils. The core is named Melyn.

photos.caption: Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 750 (31 March 2023), parked at Berea.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 748 (29 March 2023), parked at Berea.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 743 (24 March 2023), parked at Berea.

name: Belva crater
summary: Belva is an impact crater 0.9 km wide inside Jezero. Perseverance parked just west of its rim in April 2023 and photographed the layers of rock in its walls.
detail: A crater like this works as a natural road cut. One stack of steeply tilted layers may be a large sandbar, left by a river that once flowed into Jezero's lake. The rover took 152 Mastcam-Z images here on sol 772.

photos.caption: Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 772 (22 April 2023), parked at Echo Creek, on the west rim of Belva crater.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 772 (22 April 2023), parked at Echo Creek, on the west rim of Belva crater.

name: Bunsen Peak
summary: Bunsen Peak is a rock about 1.7 m wide and 1 m high that stands above the ground around it. It is about three quarters carbonate grains, cemented by almost pure silica.
detail: Both minerals are very good at keeping traces of microbes, if any lived here. The rock belongs to the margin unit along the inside of the crater rim, which may have formed on the shore of the old lake. The core, Comet Geyser, was drilled on 12 March 2024.

photos.caption: Navcam view from Perseverance on sol 1085 (9 March 2024), parked at Bunsen Peak.
Navcam view from Perseverance on sol 1085 (9 March 2024), parked at Bunsen Peak.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1085 (9 March 2024), parked at Bunsen Peak.

name: Neretva Vallis
summary: Neretva Vallis is the dry river channel that carried water into Jezero crater billions of years ago. Perseverance drove into it in mid 2024 and stopped at Mount Washburn, a hill covered with boulders.
detail: Some boulders here are of a kind not seen on Mars before. One pale, speckled boulder, named Atoko Point, stands out from all the rest. The channel is about 400 m wide, and the rover crossed a field of sand dunes in it to save time.

photos.caption: Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1164 (29 May 2024), parked at Mount Washburn in Neretva Vallis.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1164 (29 May 2024), parked at Mount Washburn in Neretva Vallis.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1164 (29 May 2024), parked at Mount Washburn in Neretva Vallis.

name: Bright Angel
summary: Bright Angel is an area of pale rock outcrops at the foot of the north wall of Neretva Vallis. Perseverance reached it on 9 June 2024.
detail: The pale rock may be old bedrock uncovered by the river, or sediment that later filled the channel. The rock named Cheyava Falls was found here in July 2024.

photos.caption: Navcam view from Perseverance on sol 1178 (13 June 2024), parked at Bright Angel.
Navcam view from Perseverance on sol 1178 (13 June 2024), parked at Bright Angel.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1178 (13 June 2024), parked at Bright Angel.

name: Cheyava Falls
summary: Cheyava Falls is an arrowhead-shaped rock with millimetre-size pale spots ringed in black, like leopard spots. The spots come from chemical reactions that microbes could have used for energy, so NASA calls the rock a potential sign of ancient life, not a proven one.
detail: The rock also holds organic compounds and white veins of calcium sulfate, left by water that once ran through it. A core named Sapphire Canyon was drilled here on 21 July 2024. In 2025 a study in the journal Nature reported the iron minerals vivianite and greigite in the spots. They can form with or without life, and it will take more study to tell which happened here.

photos.caption: Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1213 (19 July 2024), parked at Cheyava Falls.

name: Lookout Hill
summary: Lookout Hill is where Perseverance came over the top of Jezero crater's rim in December 2024. The climb took about three and a half months and gained 500 m of height.
detail: The rover climbed slopes of up to 20 percent on the way. From here it drove down the far side of the rim to Witch Hazel Hill, about 450 m away.

photos.caption: Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1356 (12 December 2024), parked at Lookout Hill, on top of the crater rim.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1356 (12 December 2024), parked at Lookout Hill, on top of the crater rim.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1356 (12 December 2024), parked at Lookout Hill, on top of the crater rim.

name: Witch Hazel Hill
summary: Witch Hazel Hill is a slope about 135 m tall on the outer side of Jezero's rim, with layer on layer of very old rock. Perseverance studied it for more than four months from December 2024.
detail: The first core here, Silver Mountain, came from a rock that most likely formed at least 3.9 billion years ago. A second rock, Tablelands, is made almost entirely of serpentine minerals, which form when a lot of water reacts with rock that cooled from magma.

photos.caption: Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1402 (29 January 2025), parked at Shallow Bay on Witch Hazel Hill.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1402 (29 January 2025), parked at Shallow Bay on Witch Hazel Hill.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1402 (29 January 2025), parked at Shallow Bay on Witch Hazel Hill.

name: Krokodillen
summary: Krokodillen is a rocky plateau of about 30 hectares, downslope from Witch Hazel Hill. Its rocks formed before Jezero crater existed and are among the oldest on Mars.
detail: The rover found clay minerals in this bedrock. Clays need liquid water to form, so they point to water here very early in the planet's history. The name means 'the crocodile' in Norwegian, after a mountain ridge on the island of Prins Karls Forland.

photos.caption: Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1554 (4 July 2025), parked on the Krokodillen plateau.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1554 (4 July 2025), parked on the Krokodillen plateau.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1554 (4 July 2025), parked on the Krokodillen plateau.

name: Valinor Hills
summary: Ingenuity's 72nd and last flight ended here on 18 January 2024, when a hard landing damaged its rotor blades. The helicopter is still at this spot, which its team named Valinor Hills.
detail: Ingenuity was built to make no more than five test flights. It flew 72 times in almost three years. Perseverance photographed it from about 415 m away on sol 1068.

photos.caption: Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1068 (21 February 2024), from about 415 m away. Ingenuity is the small dark object on the sand near the top left.
Mastcam-Z view from Perseverance on sol 1068 (21 February 2024), parked about 415 m from Valinor Hills, where Ingenuity stands.

name: Roubion (sample 1)
summary: Roubion is sample 1 of the Perseverance mission: a tube of Martian air, sealed on sol 164 after the rock Roubion crumbled during coring. The tube is at the Three Forks sample depot.
detail: The first coring attempt, at the rock Roubion in Polygon Valley on sol 164. The rock crumbled, so the sealed tube holds Martian air. Sealed on sol 164 (Aug. 6, 2021). Left at the Three Forks sample depot.

name: Montdenier (sample 2)
summary: Montdenier is sample 2 of the Perseverance mission: a rock core drilled from Rochette on sol 194. NASA lists the rock type as igneous, and the tube is at the Three Forks sample depot.
detail: Rock core from Rochette, Artuby Ridge, taken on sol 194. Sealed on sol 194 (Sept. 6, 2021). Left at the Three Forks sample depot.

detail: Rock core from Rochette, Artuby Ridge, taken on sol 196. Sealed on sol 196 (Sept. 8, 2021). Carried on the rover.
